questions.enonce_markdown: Draw a large and neatly labelled diagram of the male gamete (sperm cell) *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
A large, neat diagram of a single sperm cell, drawn in three regions from left to right, with label lines:

- **Head**: oval, containing the **nucleus** (haploid, with the chromosomes) and, at the tip, the **acrosome** (a cap containing enzymes that digest the egg membrane).
- **Middle piece**: short and thick, containing a **spiral of mitochondria** that supply energy (ATP) for swimming, and a centriole.
- **Tail (flagellum)**: long and thin, whose whip-like movement propels the sperm.
- The **cell membrane** surrounding the whole cell.

A title (for example "Human sperm cell") and a pencil drawing with no shading are expected.

questions.enonce_markdown: State four female secondary sexual characteristics. *(4 marks)*

Define the following terms as used in genetics, giving an example in each case;

(i) Genotype (ii) Phenotype. *(2, 2 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Genotype** is the genetic make-up of an organism, that is, the combination of alleles it carries for a characteristic. *Example:* $I^BI^O$ (or $Tt$).

(ii) **Phenotype** is the observable (physical or physiological) characteristic of an organism, resulting from its genotype and the environment. *Example:* blood group B (or tall plant).

questions.enonce_markdown:
A woman whose blood group was O married a man with blood group B.

(i) Explain using appropriate genetic symbols and diagrams, how it is possible for the couple to have a child with blood group O.

(ii) What is the probability or chance of their first child being blood group B? *(5 , 1 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Symbols:** $I^A$ and $I^B$ are codominant alleles and both are dominant over $I^O$, which is recessive.

(i) The woman has blood group O, so her genotype must be $I^OI^O$ (homozygous recessive). The man has blood group B, so his genotype may be $I^BI^B$ or $I^BI^O$. A child can be group O ($I^OI^O$) only if it receives an $I^O$ allele from each parent. So the father must be **heterozygous, $I^BI^O$**.

| | |
|---|---|
| Parental phenotypes | Blood group O $\times$ Blood group B |
| Parental genotypes | $I^OI^O$ $\times$ $I^BI^O$ |
| Gametes | $I^O$ and $I^O$ $\times$ $I^B$ and $I^O$ |

Punnett square:

| | $I^B$ | $I^O$ |
|---|---|---|
| **$I^O$** | $I^BI^O$ | $I^OI^O$ |
| **$I^O$** | $I^BI^O$ | $I^OI^O$ |

Offspring genotypes: $I^BI^O$ and $I^OI^O$ in the ratio 1 : 1.
Offspring phenotypes: blood group B and blood group O in the ratio **1 : 1**.

So the couple can have a child of blood group O when the man is heterozygous ($I^BI^O$).

(ii) The chance of a child of blood group B is 2 out of 4, that is **$\frac{1}{2}$ = 50 %** (one chance in two). Each child is an independent event, so the probability is the same for the first child.
